scope.quote: This study examines the investor response to Form 10-K and 10-Q reports filed between 1996 and 2001.

I first assess the extent to which 10-Ks and 10-Qs are value-relevant to investors around the filing date and measure value-relevance (or investor response) as an unsigned excess daily stock return in the short window around a filing date.
The samples also include the small business (SB) version of a 10-K or 10-Q filing.
I then combine the data into a pooled timeseries, cross-sectional multiple regression model to test for incremental effects of a given factor after controlling for the presence of the others.

dependent_variable.name: ER_it (mean standardized absolute excess return)
dependent_variable.definition: For firm i at a regular Form 10-Q filing date, the mean standardized absolute excess return (SAER) over event days 0 through 2. Daily absolute excess return is the absolute difference between the firm’s CRSP daily total return and the CRSP daily value-weighted total return index. SAER divides this absolute excess return by its standard deviation over the non-information estimation days −10 to −6 and 6 to 10 around filing day 0.
dependent_variable.formula: mean(SAER over event days 0–2); SAER = |CRSP total return − CRSP value-weighted market return| / SD(|daily excess return| over event days −10 to −6 and 6 to 10)
